query:
The group decided to order pizza. What did Soo-Yeon's response to that decision reveal about her actual position, and what specifically in how she responded signals this — given that she did not object?

Options:
A. Soo-Yeon
B. Nadia
C. Lena
D. Kezia
context:
[1] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:26:00) Priya mentioned pizza for tonight. Can we do something lighter? I had a heavy lunch 😅
[2] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:13:00) so basically Soo-Yeon ran a successful theory of mind intervention tbh. she identified the barrier and reframed the proposition. elegant
[3] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:13:00) she has good taste in groups 🙂
[4] (about=Kezia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:19:00) fine with pizza 🍕
[5] (about=Priya, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:21:00) lol ok pizza it is i guess 😅 majority wins. Nadia you want in on the order?
[6] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Requests lighter food than pizza for tonight due to a heavy lunch.
[7] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Compliments Kezia's taste in groups.
[8] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t2 @2026-04-06T19:00:00) Acknowledges the house rule with a note.
[9] (about=Soo-Yeon, said_by=Lena, profile, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Lena observes Soo-Yeon ran a successful theory of mind intervention, identifying Felix's barrier and reframing the proposition.
[10] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t6 @2026-03-16T19:01:00) Group decides to order pizza for the session, with majority vote; Nadia opts out.
[11] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Tonight's snack changed from pizza to lighter options: rice crackers, hummus, and mixed nuts.
[12] (about=GROUP, said_by=Raj, group-interaction, t6 @2026-03-16T19:01:00) Food for round two to be decided; Raj brought more flatbreads.
[13] (about=GROUP, said_by=Tomasz, group-interaction, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) House assignments for Dune: Tomasz takes Atreides, Derek takes Harkonnen; Soo-Yeon and Felix still choosing.
agent_answer:
**Answer: A. Soo-Yeon**

**Her actual position:** She did not want pizza — she wanted something lighter. Her recorded stance is exactly that: *"Requests lighter food than pizza for tonight due to a heavy lunch."* So underneath the absence of an objection, her real preference was the opposite of the group's decision.

**What in her response signals this:** She never challenged the pizza choice head-on. Instead she reframed it as a personal, non-confrontational request — *"Priya mentioned pizza for tonight. Can we do something lighter? I had a heavy lunch 😅"* — i.e. a hedged question ("Can we…?") with the reason attributed to *her own* circumstances (a heavy lunch) rather than to a flaw in the group's plan. That indirect, other-oriented reframing is precisely what Lena later flagged: *"Soo-Yeon ran a successful theory of mind intervention… she identified the barrier and reframed the proposition. elegant."*

So the tell is not a stated objection but the soft, self-attributed reframe — and it was effective: the group's snack later changed from pizza to lighter options (rice crackers, hummus, mixed nuts).

query:
The group discussed the expectation that everyone should bring either a game or food to the annual marathon. What did Nadia's response signal about her actual relationship to this group norm, and how would you know from what she said?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Tomasz
C. Marcus
D. Lena
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:06:00) I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.
[2] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
[3] (about=Priya, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:07:00) that totally counts Nadia! honestly a good game pitch is worth more than another bag of chips 😊
[4] (about=Lena, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:10:00) so basically that explains why Nadia didn't push back on Tomasz's Dune ruling even though everyone else was complaining tbh
[5] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:38:00) I did not want to interrupt the game.
[6] (about=Nadia, core, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Explains she did not want to interrupt the game, hence not mentioning the food issue.
[7] (about=Nadia, core, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Will bring a game to the marathon but does not participate in food arrangement.
[8] (about=Nadia, core, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Thanks Soo-Yeon for flagging the food issue, noting she noticed it as well but did not say anything.
[9] (about=Nadia, said_by=Lena, profile, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Lena suggests that Nadia's lack of pushback on Tomasz's Dune ruling is explained by their shared wargame history.
agent_answer:
**A. Nadia**

Nadia signaled that she **accepts part of the group norm but not the food side of it**: she said she **would bring a game**, but explicitly said **“I do not participate in the food arrangement.”** So she relates to the norm by meeting it through the game contribution while opting out of shared food duties.

How we know: from her own words — *“I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.”* Her later explanation that she **didn’t want to interrupt the game** also suggests she prioritized the game over raising the food issue, rather than rejecting the whole group norm.
